Our complete team of twelve would have closed in by the time that the 60th man was home - surely a performance of which even the wildest optimist would never have dreamed.

Another Belgrave/Selsonia union involved your co-Editor Alan Mead, who also managed to get into a London "glossy". The other half of the Editorship takes this opportunity of wishing Pat and Alan a happy future.

Belated congratulations to ARNOLD BENTT and PAT on their engagement. Pat has supported us at several of our league fixtures and is already used to the strange ways of athletes, her brother being Herne Hill's talented javelin thrower Neville Wade.
I must make special mention of the track and field section with its wonderful team spirit, led by the never complaining Alan Mead, well assisted by Pat.
Belated congratulations to two Belgravians who have taken the marital plunge. Howard Satchell (can he really be 20 years a member) has married Chris from Canada, and Arnold Bentt has married Pat.

Lionel leads Bob Smith, Dick Piotrowski, and Adrian Major during the Belgrave 7½ miles Cross Country Championship of 1968 but all four had to give way to Tony Fairclough (1st), Laurie O'Hara (2nd) and Pat O'Connor (3rd) by the finish.
It was Terry, the shorter distance half of the racing Newell brothers. Both Pat and Terry Newell are still with us to this day. For every race after that initial road relay, Tony was an A team man.
At Pat’s tea afterwards, you won’t be dining alone.
Well done to the gutsy girls, and humble thanks to the support staff. Pat, your lemon cake has me hallucinating ... oh when will I see her again?

Finally I would like to thank Belgrave and in particular Alan and Pat for giving me some great running memories during my time at Belgrave Harriers, and I would be delighted to run the odd race for Belgrave whenever I come over to the UK for the occasional visit.
He also met up with contemporaries, such as John Martin, George Flanaghan, and Pat & Alan Mead, (who were not of course married at that time)
